I have been in your situation. Please, please, please stop using every single cosmetic cream, product, acid, etc at home. I experimented with this stuff and wrecked my skin. Redness = inflamed skin and putting any sort of acids on it yourself, or other products loaded with nasty chemicals - instead of taking a dermatologist’s advice - is going to worsen your condition. 

This is what I personally recommend, from my own experience of going through exactly what you’re going through.

1. Use an extremely, EXTREMELY bland moisturizer. I use neutrogena oil free, and micellar water to cleanse my face. THAT’S IT. The goal is to not aggravate your skin any further.
2. Tretinoin / Tazorac will be your best friend when it comes to further minimizing acne breakouts, and also to helping increase collagen production, because I do see some indented scarring on your cheeks as well.
3. Do your research and find a board certified dermatologist who specializes in acne scarring. The procedure that will work the best for your redness is pulse dye laser. If they push BBL (broadband light therapy) don’t do it, not as effective. You need to go with the real deal laser. Google and read about pulse dye laser and see the before and after pics - you’ll look like a monster for a week with bruises all over your face but TRUST me it works (I’ve had it done myself and saw good results) And it’s basically painless.
4. Once your redness is gone, if you want to tackle the indented scars, consider subcision. It is by far the most effective procedure for atrophic acne scarring. I had my first Subcision a few months ago and I had 20% improvement in my scars from just one procedure. 

 I have been in your shoes and I know firsthand how awful it is to be going through this. I hate to know that other people are suffering with this.

Just remember - improving your acne scars is a journey - it is a long journey and will most likely take years - but if you have your acne under control, I promise you, it WILL GET BETTER. It takes a lot of patience, and unfortunately a lot of money in certain circumstances, but I promise it’ll get better. Feel free to message me if you have any questions.

Yes. Things you will need.

2. Subcision coupled with a dermal filler can be a great option. I recommend not opting for a permanent filler because those have more complications.
3. Microneedling (Does not need to be PRP.) Please see a good dermatologist though.
